CONFIRMED_CONTENT: What is stated: `NavierStokes.SmoothPowerMomentMatrix.Family` (NavierStokes/SmoothPowerMomentMatrix.lean:93), fields `bump_nonnegative` (line 106) and `bump_support` (line 108) at every p ∈ U; `Family.compact_inverse_jets_bound` (line 197) takes `hU : IsOpen U`, `hK : IsCompact K`, `hKU : K ⊆ U`. Same fields and hypotheses in NavierStokes/SmoothExponentialMomentMatrix.lean:22 and :98.

Where the sign fields are used: `exponent_injective`, `separated`, `bump_nonnegative`, `bump_nonzero` occur only in `Family.matrix_det_ne_zero` (NavierStokes/SmoothPowerMomentMatrix.lean:167-176; NavierStokes/SmoothExponentialMomentMatrix.lean:69-78), at the single point p. The bodies of `integrand_contDiffOn` (SmoothPowerMomentMatrix.lean:130-151) and `matrix_contDiffOn` (:153-165) use only `exponent_smooth`, `bump_smooth`, `lower_continuous`, `upper_continuous`, `lower_pos`, `bump_support`.

Stated declarations that close the difference for K = Icc (-1) 1:
- `NavierStokes.GenericEndpointExtension.closedStripExtension` (NavierStokes/GenericEndpointExtension.lean:761), for f with `ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ f closedStrip`, `closedStrip = Icc (-1) 1 ×ˢ univ` (:564); `closedStripExtension_eq` (:766, equals f on the strip); `closedStripExtension_contDiff` (:775, globally `ContDiff ℝ ∞`); `closedStripExtension_zero` (:793, a fibre that vanishes for all t ∈ Icc (-1) 1 vanishes for all real t).
- `NavierStokes.UniformCone.positive_uniform_margin` (NavierStokes/UniformCone.lean:29): a positive continuous function on a compact set has a positive lower bound.
- `NavierStokes.SmoothPowerMomentMatrix.integral_contDiffOn_of_moving_support` (NavierStokes/SmoothPowerMomentMatrix.lean:25): a general lemma about an arbitrary F on an open U, with no sign hypothesis.
- `NavierStokes.PowerMomentMatrix.bumpMomentMatrix_det_ne_zero` (NavierStokes/PowerMomentMatrix.lean:261) and `NavierStokes.ExponentialMomentMatrix.expBumpMomentMatrix_det_ne_zero` (NavierStokes/ExponentialMomentMatrix.lean:72): pointwise det ≠ 0.
- `NavierStokes.SmoothPowerMomentMatrix.determinant_contDiffOn` (:52) and `inverse_contDiffOn` (:66); the latter is stated for an arbitrary set U, with no openness hypothesis.
- Body of `Family.compact_inverse_jet_bound` / `compact_inverse_jets_bound` (:184-207): continuity of the jets on an open set, then `IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn`.

Lemma A.2 side: `NavierStokes.ClosedIntervalMomentRepair.Data` (NavierStokes/ClosedIntervalMomentRepair.lean:16) takes `hB : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ B I` and `invertible : ∀ x ∈ I, (B x).IsInvertible`, with `I = Icc (-1) 1` (NavierStokes/ClosedIntervalCk.lean:23); `inverseNorm` is defined from them (:38) and `inverseNorm_zero` (:48) identifies it with the pointwise supremum. Only `ParameterizedMomentRepair.exists_smooth_uniform_branch` (NavierStokes/ParameterizedMomentRepair.lean:16) takes `hBn` as a hypothesis, and I found no user of it outside its own file.

No `Family` is constructed anywhere: the two namespaces occur only in their own files and in an import at NavierStokes/PaperAdditionalResults.lean:17. A word-search for sorry, admit, axiom and native_decide in the eight files cited here (the two extension files, the four moment-matrix files, UniformCone.lean, ParametricRephase.lean) found nothing.

ATTRIBUTION_GAP: NavierStokes/PowerMomentMatrix.lean:261 (`bumpMomentMatrix_det_ne_zero`) and NavierStokes/ExponentialMomentMatrix.lean:72 (`expBumpMomentMatrix_det_ne_zero`); neither mentions the other, and nothing bundles them with the parametric clause.

CONVENTION: `bumpMomentMatrix` (NavierStokes/PowerMomentMatrix.lean:252) is `fun i j => ∫ t, t ^ a i * β j t` over ℝ; the identification with ∫ t in Ioi 0 appears only as `Family.matrix_eq_positive_integral` (NavierStokes/SmoothPowerMomentMatrix.lean:120), which needs a `Family`.

Clauses (i) and (ii) are stated in Lean more generally than in the paper: continuity replaces smoothness, support in the closed interval replaces support in the interior, any finite size and arbitrary distinct real exponents are allowed, and the exponential clause imposes no sign condition on the intervals. Clause (iii) is stated only for a `Family` on an open U whose nonnegativity and support fields hold at every p ∈ U (NavierStokes/SmoothPowerMomentMatrix.lean:93, :197; NavierStokes/SmoothExponentialMomentMatrix.lean:22, :98), and paper data given only on a compact parameter set need not extend to such a family, so that theorem cannot always be instantiated. The clause nevertheless follows from stated declarations for the paper's parameter set, η ∈ [-1,1] (p.34, p.127). `GenericEndpointExtension.closedStripExtension` (NavierStokes/GenericEndpointExtension.lean:761, with `_eq` :766, `_contDiff` :775, `_zero` :793) extends the bumps and exponents to globally smooth data with supports in fixed intervals, once `UniformCone.positive_uniform_margin` (NavierStokes/UniformCone.lean:29) bounds the endpoints. The bodies of `integrand_contDiffOn` and `matrix_contDiffOn` (SmoothPowerMomentMatrix.lean:130-165) repeat for the extended data because they use no sign, nonvanishing, injectivity or separation field. `bumpMomentMatrix_det_ne_zero` (NavierStokes/PowerMomentMatrix.lean:261) is applied pointwise on [-1,1] only, and `inverse_contDiffOn` (SmoothPowerMomentMatrix.lean:66) holds on an arbitrary set; compactness then bounds each derivative as in lines 184-207. This is a recombination of about a dozen steps with proof-body repetition and Mathlib glue, read and not compiled, so the verdict is SINGLE_SOURCE_OK with relation different_formulation and a low finding for the open-domain packaging. It does not cover data that are smooth only intrinsically on a compact set that is not an interval; the repository states no Whitney-type extension, and the paper neither defines smoothness on such a set nor uses one. The paper's later argument does not use the moving-data generality: Lemma A.2 (p.127) assumes an abstract smooth invertible B on [-1,1], and the applications read (pp. 42, 140) have fixed bumps and exponents with η entering as a scalar row factor, which clause (i) and the repository's constant-matrix lemmas cover.

findings.summary: The Lean states clause (iii) only for a `Family` on an open U, with nonnegativity and support required at every p ∈ U, and paper data given only on a compact parameter set need not extend to such a family. For the paper's own parameter set, η ∈ [-1,1] (p.34, p.127), the clause still follows from stated declarations by a recombination of about a dozen steps through the stated extension `closedStripExtension`; I read that derivation and did not compile it, and it does not cover data given only on a compact set that is not an interval.
No single declaration states Lemma A.1. Clauses (i) and (ii) are two theorems in two files, each at greater generality than the paper; they conjoin by logic alone, so this part is packaging only.

The Lean matrices integrate over all of ℝ, not the paper's (0,∞). They agree because the stated support hypothesis makes the integrand vanish off Icc (l j) (u j) ⊂ (0,∞), but that identification is stated only for `Family` data.
